content.thinking:
I'm planning out the whole module carefully before writing anything, designing a hunched swamp troll with Blizzard-style proportions — oversized hands and head, teal-green skin, a mohawk of red-orange bristles, tusks, and bone fetish accessories like necklaces and belts.

Now I'm working out the skeleton setup, placing the pelvis root and chaining the spine from hips to chest to neck to head with specific coordinates for a slightly hunched upright stance, keeping the construction simple and robust so I'm confident in how the chain and joint names will resolve.

Actually simpler to work in absolute model coordinates for the head rather than chaining local frames — I'll set a head center and neck end point directly, then attach jaw and other parts to the head bone using absolute coordinates to avoid confusion. For the torso, I'm considering building it as a loft following the spine and hips joints as the bone list.

Defining torso stations...

I'm tapering the neck sweep down to a thinner radius and tinting it skin-colored, then placing the head joint angled forward off the neck, followed by a jaw joint aimed downward for an underbite look. For the head shape itself, I'm sketching a wide skull as a scaled sphere with a heavy brow ridge capsule sitting over where the eyes would go.

Now I'm detailing the face: small glowing yellow eyes tucked under the brow, a wide flat snout with nostrils, and a chunky protruding lower jaw box to emphasize the underbite. I'm adding curved tusk sweeps rising from the lower jaw in bone/ivory color, plus small upper teeth, and starting to extrude long pointy troll-like ears outward from the head using a 2D outline profile.

Working out the ear outline points so the shape stays non-self-intersecting, then I'm planning a mohawk made of blade shapes extruded along a curved path running from the forehead back over the neck and down the upper back.

Adding color gradient to blade...

Working out the mohawk blade orientation vectors to keep thickness and lean axes properly perpendicular...

Head blades get a smaller lean angle (15-30°) toward vertical, while back blades lean further (50-70°), each attached to the appropriate bone -- head joint versus spine for the back row.

For positioning, I'll use raycasting against the torso and skull surfaces to find actual hit points for blade placement, so the mohawk follows the body contour down the back and across the scalp rather than relying on approximate z-offsets.

I'm planning the eyes as glowing yellow with tiny dark pupils, a heavy brow sweep in darker skin tone, and warts scattered across the torso using surface scattering with minimum distance spacing, each stuck down with slight embedding. Now I'm moving on to the oversized arms and shoulder joints.

For the hand I'm sketching a fist with tapering arm radii, four finger capsules plus a thumb with claw spikes, attached at the wrist tip and oriented hanging downward with a small palm box.

I'll keep fingers rigid on the wrist without extra joints for simplicity. For shoulders, I'm adding a hide-and-bone pauldron plus a muscular sphere bulge at both shoulder joints, keeping it symmetric for now. Moving to legs, I'm placing hips at the sides and planning plantigrade, thick troll legs down to the foot targets.

Working out the hip-knee-ankle chain with forward-bent knees, then adding a wider foot box with three clawed toe spheres, making sure the foot bottom sits flush on the ground plane. I'm also setting a tapered sweep radius along the leg chain so the thighs are thicker than the ankles.

Now I'm placing the hips joint and pelvis, and starting on the loincloth geometry, sketching a hanging front flap as a simple outline shape from the belt downward.

I'm reasoning that the root joint keeps the default +Y orientation, so a belt loop around the hips at y=1.05 should use that direction. But I realize the thigh tubes' rounded caps extend up to about y=1.15, meaning a loop at y=1.05 could end up slicing through both the torso and the thighs instead of isolating just the waist.

Checking: picking a loop centered at x=0 correctly selects the torso surface since the thigh positions don't enclose that axis, so applying the sweep for a belt with leather coloring to just the torso sweep should work fine. I want to add a belt buckle decoration -- a small skull made from a sphere, jaw box, and eye sockets, so I'm planning a reusable fetishSkull helper, plus extending the idea into a necklace loop of bone/skull fetishes around the neck.

Now I'm working through a chest necklace: cutting a loop at the shoulder height on the torso surface only, then draping a thin cord loop slightly raised, and hanging bone and tooth shapes from frames sampled along that path -- alternating spikes and small bones, with a larger centerpiece skull placed at the front using a ray cast against the torso surface.

I'm also sketching an alternative drape approach: a closed catmull curve running from one shoulder down to a low front point and back up around the neck, letting it pull toward the nearest body surface for a natural hang.

I'll account for the neck not being part of the torso surface, so the drape target needs to include a neck sweep as well, then place beads along the draped cord using tangent-aligned hanging spikes for the teeth.

I want to restrict where teeth hang to the lower front portion of the closed path, using a from/to range around t=0.08 to 0.62 so items avoid the back and mohawk area. I'm also considering adding bone bangles or a fetish staff as extra accessories.

I'll skip giving it a weapon and instead hang a prominent skull on one side of the belt and a pouch on the other, then focus on the skin paint—using a mottled teal base with darker belly tones and warm-to-cool lighting across the body.

Writing skin paint function...

Still refining the color mixing logic...

I want to double-check the smoothstep edge reversal math works correctly for the mud blending near the feet, then move on to adding glowing yellow eyes and tattoo/war paint detailing using the same shared skin paint for visual continuity.

Thinking through decal placement for tribal war-paint — considering a cream-white spiral/handprint decal on the chest using an SVG texture, and possibly adding face stripes or a head decal for additional war-paint detail.

Tusks could be curved upward from the lower jaw, with simple geometry for gums, dark red mouth interior, and small box-shaped teeth rows along the jawline.

Now I'm laying out the head's precise feature coordinates: the skull sphere's position and scale radii relative to the head bone, and a brow ridge built as a flattened capsule shape spanning across the forehead.

Continuing with angled scowl brows, glowing eye spheres with black pupils and dark sunken sockets, cheekbone spheres, and the start of the upper muzzle box dimensions and placement.

Still shaping the snout, nose, nostrils, and lower jaw with rounded sphere-based geometry for the chin and jaw sides, plus a dark mouth interior cavity.

Now I'm checking the head's spatial proportions so the jaw juts forward for the underbite without clipping through the muzzle, and positioning the tusks so they emerge from the jaw sides and rise outward past the muzzle's width.

Instead of a torus, I'll add a small gold band by sweeping a short rod along the tusk's bezier path, matching its radius at that point so it sits snugly as a ring. The tusks curve slightly up and back, the neck stays thick and mostly hidden between the shoulders, and the head sits forward of the torso for that hunched posture.

Now I'm shaping the torso: a trapezius hump near the shoulders, pectoral spheres on the chest, and a pot-belly sphere lower down, all attached to spine joint bones. I'm adding a pelvis part at the hips and starting the shoulder ball joints for the arm chain.

Working out the hunched arm pose: computing distances for the upper arm and forearm to reach a hand target in front of the body, bending the elbow backward with an IK plane hint. I'm tuning the chain's tube radii along the arm from shoulder to wrist so it tapers naturally into the hand.

Now I'm thinking through a forearm bracer design, considering a lathed cuff shape with a rectangular cross-section outline positioned partway down the forearm, oriented along the limb's direction.

Chain joints run shoulder-elbow-wrist with the tip included last. For the cuff I'm thinking leather brown with bone studs, plus adding a second armband ring higher up with bone tooth spikes, lathed near the upper arm at t≈0.3.

Still working out the spike placement geometry... Writing ring and spike code...

Now for hands: I'll compute direction from elbow to wrist to position the hand center slightly past the wrist, then build the palm as a scaled sphere oriented along that direction, working through how scale composes with rotation in the local frame.

Writing finger capsule placement...

Shaping the tapered claw at each fingertip with a dark bone material, then positioning the thumb inward toward the body with its own curl so it reads naturally against the palm, anchoring everything relative to the wrist joint.

Now moving to the legs: hiding the forearm cap inside the palm, then building the foot as a smoothed, scaled sphere at the ankle target with three forward-pointing toe capsules plus claws, keeping the base flush with the floor.

Adjusting leg sweep radii and adding a small spike at the knee for bone detail, positioned using the IK joint data. I'm also starting on the loincloth with front and back flaps extruded from the hip bone.

I'm checking that the belly sphere doesn't collide with the front flap placement -- shrinking the belly scale slightly so the flap can hang properly from a belt loop around the torso instead of clipping through the belly geometry.

I'll move the belt down to y≈0.99 so it sits below the belly overhang, then extrude the flap from there, thin and hanging to about y 0.45, positioned just outside the thighs at z 0.24 so it doesn't intersect them.

For the rear flap, I'll mirror the front setup at z -0.24, matching the thigh backs so the outline stays symmetric.

I'm also thinking through decoration for the loincloth—adding bone trim spikes along the bottom edge and a painted leather texture with stripes, patches, and a darker bottom band plus a red trim stripe using a paint function based on position.

Now I'm sketching out a skull helper that builds the cranium, jaw, eye sockets, and nose as separate parts, each oriented using a quaternion derived from the facing direction so offsets rotate correctly with the skull.

Next I'm planning a fetish bundle hanging off the belt — a cord strung with small skulls and feathers dangling from the left hip.

Still working out the feather geometry...

I also want small wart spheres scattered across the torso, and shoulder pauldrons made from a lathed leather dome tilted outward along the shoulder's axis, sitting at the joint point.

Positioning the dome over the shoulder muscle, then adding bone spikes in a ring around its rim, angled outward with a slight upward tilt to form a cone-like cluster of spikes.

Beyond the spikes, I'm considering chest war paint and a bone necklace, deciding the bandolier detail isn't needed since the necklace and paint cover it. Now I'm sketching the mohawk ridge, tracing its sweep from the front of the skull toward the top.

Continuing the crest path down into the neck, I'm sinking the base ridge points slightly below the surface and sketching the back-of-torso blade placement, falling back to skip if the ray doesn't hit.

Now I'm defining the blade geometry itself: smaller sizes along the back row, thinner heads, and a jagged spiky outline shape that I'll scale to each blade's height.

I'll use a shared mohawk paint function with fixed absolute height thresholds for yellow/orange/red bands rather than per-blade relative ones, since blade heights are small and consistent. Skipping extra bone rings or skull details on the head to keep things simple.

Now I'm working out small torus-shaped earrings in gold or bone sitting at the ear tips, oriented flat in the XY plane so they read as circles from the front, plus tooth-shaped earrings hanging below as spikes. I'm positioning the ears themselves outward and upward from the head using an extruded outline shape.

For the eyes I'll use a glow effect with dark pupils inside, and for the chest I'm designing a bone-white war paint decal as an SVG with spiral and zigzag strokes mimicking hand-print and slash markings, sized small enough to read clearly on the pectorals.

I'm figuring out where to place the decal, combining the torso and pec parts into a single surface target so the paint wraps correctly across the chest, and positioning it roughly at belly height so it reads as centered body paint rather than disappearing behind the pec spheres.

I'm also planning scattered warts across the torso using a filtered surface scatter so they avoid facing directly backward, and thinking through adding a bone fetish bundle hanging off the back with a skull poking above the shoulder as a distinctive troll accessory.

For the totem, I'm positioning a mounted pole diagonally across the back so a large skull with feathers and a hanging teeth cord pokes above the shoulder from the front view, connected to the back with a couple of small lashing cylinders rather than a draped strap to keep it simple.

Checking proportions: with the mohawk and pole combined the figure reaches about 2.5m, which feels right for a stooped troll frame.

Now I'm placing a skull motif on the belt buckle too.

Adjusting the belly position to center around y 1.25 so it clears the belt at y .97, with radii .29/.22/.2 giving a front z of about .47 at that height.

Now I'm figuring out the belt placement at y .97 against the pelvis station, adding a skull buckle in front with a bone-colored material, and hanging a flap extruding downward from the belt. I'm also checking that the pelvis sphere at hip height doesn't poke through the torso surface near the belt region, since its width could exceed the torso loft there.

Tightening the pelvis sphere scale down to [0.26, 0.18, 0.2] so the belt stays visible at the sides rather than hidden. Now I'm mapping out the spine chain's joint positions for the torso loft, making sure the loft path starting point aligns properly with where the first joint projects onto the chain.

Working through the loft station widths and depths from hips to shoulders, keeping the chest broad at width 1.0 while the shoulders sit narrower at x=.55. Then I'm defining the neck chain as a child of the chest joint, setting up its three-point sweep with a tapering radius, and starting to position the head joint off the end of the neck chain.

I'll apply a small forward-down rotation to the jaw joint, around 9-10 degrees, to open the mouth slightly for a natural gap between the teeth -- doing this as a final pose adjustment after all the geometry is built so it doesn't interfere with anything else.

Now I'm placing the teeth: upper row fixed to the head, lower row attached to the jaw, spaced along the front rim in a slight arc so they align into a believable bite.

I'm simplifying this by placing the lower front teeth to poke out just before the muzzle line, adjusting the chin sphere's position and scale so the front edge sits around y1.9, then positioning the lower incisors' base accordingly.

Defining more colors...

Setting up gradient-based paint functions for bone and tusks, mixing lighter and darker tones with noise for a weathered look.

Now I'm sketching out the leather paint shader with noise and top-lightening, confirming skin paint reuse for arms, then planning the full TypeScript imports needed—THREE, builder helpers, limb/bezier/catmull utilities, paint helpers, and the vector type.

Setting up imports...

Still writing helper functions...

Adding neck, head, jaw joints, then starting a loop for symmetric arm joints with shoulder positions mirrored across sides.

Still building the arm sweep and hand frame, computing forearm direction and palm orientation from the wrist bone...

Still writing claw spike parameters...

Now I'm working out the thumb placement, figuring out which direction is "inward" relative to each arm side so the thumb base and curl path point toward the palm correctly.

Next I'm designing a wrist cuff using a lathed rectangular profile attached to the forearm's bone and tangent, checking that the chain point's position/tangent types line up with the lathe function's expected axis and anchor parameters.

Then I'm adding stud rings around the wrist (short spikes arranged circularly via the ring helper) and a matching tooth band higher up the arm, using spikes and another leather cuff lathe at a different point along the chain.

I interpolate the band radius at that position to figure out where the spikes should sit relative to the cuff wall, settling on a ring radius of .18. Then I add a shoulder muscle ellipsoid anchored to the arm's first joint, and start blocking out a pauldron as a lathed dome shape with a normalized axis direction and an outline profile beginning at the shoulder point.

Now I'm figuring out the full outline for the pauldron's solid shape, closing it back along the axis, and deciding to attach it to the arm's shoulder joint so it follows the limb when raised, colored as painted leather. I'm also adding a rim of studs as a ring object positioned slightly above the base along the axis, with eight studs at radius .25.

Working out gold stud cones and a second ring of larger outward spikes at radius .14, tilted to match the dome's curvature, with five spikes offset upward along the axis so they sit flush on the surface — explicitly binding this ring to the arm's shoulder joint since there's no bone default to inherit from.

Now moving to the leg geometry: setting hip and foot points for a limb chain, checking the hip-to-foot distance against the max reach to confirm the knee bends forward correctly, then building the leg chain parented to the hips with named hip and knee joints...

Adding foot and ankle placement...

Adding more claw and ankle details...

Now adding torso ellipsoids for pecs, belly, and a trapezius hump near the neck, plus setting neck sweep radii and the pelvis ellipsoid. Then I'm starting the crest path for the head blades.

Still writing blade geometry...

Coloring the mohawk tips yellow near the top and orange/red lower down, then working out the back blade placement along the torso ray — but I realize the trapezius hump juts out further back than where the blades start, so they might end up embedded inside the hump geometry instead of sitting on the surface.

Now I'm filling in the neck region connecting the head back to the hump, positioning a couple more blades along the neck path with slightly adjusted angles and heights so the mohawk reads as continuous into the hump area.

Moving on to face details, I'm planning a small gold septum ring using a thin torus geometry positioned under the nose, oriented so it reads as a circle from the front view.

I'm skipping some extras like forehead warts, brow scars, and chin tufts to keep things simple, but I'm still deciding whether to add bone spike earrings hanging from the ear tips—though I'm realizing the geometry puts the ear tip higher than the skull's top point, which needs checking.

Positioning eyes and eye sockets...

Adding glowing pupils, then checking whether the muzzle sphere's geometry overlaps the eye sockets by comparing their ellipsoid boundaries at shared coordinates.

Adjusting the chin to protrude slightly forward of the muzzle for an underbite look, repositioning lower teeth spikes and tusks so they sit outside the jaw rather than buried inside it.

Defining the tusk curve as a bezier so it arcs outward from the jaw and clears the muzzle and nostrils, keeping length modest. Now I'm moving on to other anatomy details—chest with pecs and a hump, plus a decal, and a fetish totem pole attached to the back starting from a base point behind the figure.

I'm positioning the pole from a lower-back point up to a shoulder-height point, giving it a wood-colored cylindrical sweep, then placing a scaled skull at the top and orienting it to face slightly forward so it reads as peeking over the shoulder. I'm computing points along the pole using vector interpolation, then adding a couple of lashing straps connecting the pole to the torso.

I'm also adding totem decorations: feathers sprouting near the top of the pole, hanging bone beads strung along its length using small spheres or capsules spaced at intervals to suggest vertebrae.

Now I'm figuring out a belt fetish bundle hanging from the hip, finding the attachment point via a ray cast onto the pelvis surface and then hanging a cord down from it with a small skull and feathers dangling at the end, mirrored for the left hip.

Writing bone and feather helpers...

Estimating total part counts across all the scattered features—warts, teeth, mohawk spikes, skull helpers—to confirm we're staying under budget, then double-checking paint function type signatures before writing the skin paint shader with noise-based coloring.

Writing skin paint logic...

Now mapping out the belly patch so it only appears on the torso front, using smoothstep gates on y-position and normal direction to exclude the head, arms, and legs.

Skipping muscle lines and scar decals for simplicity, I'll focus on a warm rim light and a chest tattoo detail instead. I still need to handle eye glow parts properly and double-check the arm/hand code for unused variables before composing the final TypeScript.

I also need to make sure every declared variable is actually used to avoid lint errors. For the skull helper, I'm defining a function that positions bone pieces by rotating and scaling offsets around an anchor point, then fixing the type so position tuples are strict 3-number arrays rather than a loose union type that breaks indexing.

Now I'm working out the skull geometry itself: a scaled sphere for the cranium, a box for the face, and small dark spheres for the eye sockets positioned slightly forward and offset left/right, adjusting their z-depth so they sit just in front of the cranium surface.

I'm placing a small dark sphere for the nose and a flattened box for the teeth, plus a jaw box beneath, tuning their positions until the proportions read correctly. Once the skull is settled I'll move on to the belt and other gear, then double-check that all the helper functions like frame, aim, rng, bezier, catmull, limb, svg, and glow are actually being used before writing out the final code.

I'm figuring out the tusk geometry — setting up a random seed for scatter variation, then computing band positions along the tusk curve using bezier sampling so the gold ring sits at a slightly larger radius than the tusk itself, accounting for how the polygon sides affect the circumscribed radius.

Now I'm designing the loincloth paint function, blending leather color with mottled noise and adding red trim stripes near the top and bottom edges based on surface position.

Then I'm shaping the hanging flap's outline as a zigzag polygon tapering to a V-shaped point at the bottom, with a thin extruded thickness.

Adding bone bead spikes...

Working out spike dimensions and positioning...

I'm figuring out the body part assembly order—torso, belly, hump, then pecs—feeding them into a surface that supports raycasting and decal placement, with warts scattered across using sticky collision detection.

Now I'm working on the necklace, deciding to combine torso, hump, pecs, and a neck sweep part into one unified surface so the cord drapes correctly across all of them.

For the belt loop I need it to stay confined to just the torso, since the belly's lower point sits above the waist line and pelvis isn't part of that surface group. I'm sketching the necklace's path with a closed catmull curve looping around the neck and chest, then having each point on that path snap to the nearest body surface -- near the top it should catch on the hump around the shoulders.

I'm checking that the necklace's drape doesn't clip through the pecs where the path dips toward the chest center -- the gap between the pec ellipsoids is narrow enough that the curve should just graze the torso surface there instead of sinking in. For the hanging teeth, I'm placing spikes along a portion of the draped cord using directional bone shapes, working out which segment of the path corresponds to the front-center hang point.

I want to add a centerpiece bone or skull bead at the lowest point of the drape, but pinning down that exact spot is tricky -- the path's parameter isn't evenly spaced with arc length, so t=0.4 isn't necessarily the true center-front low point. I'm weighing whether to brute-force it with a ray-cast against the torso mesh or just find the closest-t estimate directly on the cord curve.

Using `cord.closestT` against the known front-center position to get the right parameter, then placing teeth and a skull bead relative to that point using the path's position vector, offset slightly down and forward for the skull. I'm confirming the drape function and glow import are set up correctly, then placing the topmost skull on the totem at a larger scale, and filling in a bead ring along the cord with alternating bone and red materials.

Now I'm working through the remaining totem details: lashing rods connecting cord points to hit targets (handling the null case), a right-hip fetish object, and finally posing the jaw before returning the root. I'm defining a small ellipsoid helper using a sphere geometry scaled per-axis, confirming the part and spike function overloads accept color and bone options correctly, and deciding how to convert Vector3 values into plain array coordinates for these calls.

Writing body part placement loops...
